short.bigTake: Cautious, risk-off tilt heading into the busiest week of the quarter. Big tech is being sold on AI-spending worries (Nasdaq −0.7%, second losing week, ~6% off its high) while money rotates into energy, health care, staples and small caps. Oil near $103 WTI keeps inflation and rate-hike fears alive. Everything this week funnels into Wednesday: the Fed at 2:00 p.m. and Microsoft and Alphabet after the close, then Amazon, GDP and core PCE on Thursday.
bullets: Tone: risk-off but not panicked. SPY −0.4%, QQQ −0.8% last week, both below their 50-day averages; the equal-weight S&P beat the S&P by 1.6 points and small caps rose 2%, so the selling is concentrated in mega-cap tech, not everywhere.

The AI trade is the pressure point: Meta −9.4% and Alphabet −6.0% last week after Meta raised its spending plan and Tesla cut its; Nvidia and Broadcom are below their 50-day averages. Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon decide whether that worry deepens or eases.

Fed Wednesday 2:00 p.m.: a hold at 3.75–4.00% is priced (about 93% on prediction markets) after September's hike; the risk is the press conference leaning toward a December hike (about 76% priced) because CPI is 3.7% and oil is above $100.
Thursday 8:30 a.m. is the second big macro moment: GDP (3.2% expected) and core PCE (0.3% m/m expected). A hot PCE on top of a hawkish Fed would hit tech hardest.

Oil: Brent hit $116.72 Friday (highest close since April) on Iran-strike reports; it eased Monday on diplomacy talk. Energy is the strongest sector and reports this week (Exxon, Chevron Friday; Shell, TotalEnergies Thursday; Phillips 66 Wednesday).
Options are pricing large moves: ServiceNow ±10%, Intel ±10%, KLA ±9%, Seagate ±10%, Corning ±10%, Amazon ±7.8%, Alphabet ±6%, Microsoft ±5.3%.

full.mainEvent: Fed Wed 2:00 p.m. + MSFT/GOOGL after the close
full.bigTake: The market enters the heaviest week of earnings season in a risk-off tilt, but it is a rotation more than a rout. Mega-cap tech and the AI trade are being sold on spending worries (Meta's higher capex plan, Tesla's lower one), pushing the Nasdaq 100 to its second straight weekly loss and about 6% below its record. At the same time the equal-weight S&P, small caps, energy, health care and staples rose. Oil near $103 WTI and $117 Brent, with Iran headlines, keeps inflation expectations high (1-year expectations 4.7%) and keeps the Fed on a hiking path: a hold is priced for Wednesday, but a December hike is the base case. The week's outcome hinges on three things in about 36 hours: the Fed's tone Wednesday at 2:30, Microsoft and Alphabet that evening, and GDP/core PCE plus Amazon on Thursday. A hawkish Fed plus weak cloud numbers is the bad combination for tech; good cloud growth with spending discipline could spark a relief rally in the most-sold names.

tape.summary: Stocks slipped for a second week, with the damage in tech and communication services. Thursday's Nasdaq drop (−2.6%, biggest since June) came the day after Meta and Tesla reported. The 10-year yield eased from about 5.10% to 4.99% despite hot price data, VIX finished just under 20 (it touched 22 the week before), oil kept climbing on Iran, gold fell to a three-month low as rate-hike bets firmed, and the dollar held near its 52-week high.

macro.summary: Last week's data said the economy is running hot, not cooling: claims at their lowest since July, business surveys strong with selling prices rising at the fastest pace since 2022, while consumers feel terrible (sentiment second-lowest on record) and expect 4.7% inflation. Together with September's 3.7% CPI (released Oct 14), that is why markets expect another hike in December. The stock market's reaction last week was driven more by earnings (Meta, Tesla) and oil than by the data itself; yields actually eased over the week.

trend.earningsImplication: In this tape, tech misses are likely to be punished harder than beats are rewarded, especially for names already below their 50-day (Alphabet, Meta's peers, Broadcom, Nvidia). Last quarter the big reporters beat 82% of the time, so a beat alone may not be enough; spending plans and guidance will decide the move. Defensive and energy names entering in uptrends have more room for 'good news, stock up'.
